question.text: Which regulator is responsible for the National Pension System (NPS) and other pension schemes in India?

answer.text: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)
Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) under the PFRDA Act 2013
Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 1.1.4 (v), PFRDA regulates the NPS and other pension schemes under the PFRDA Act 2013. IRDAI regulates insurance, SEBI regulates securities, RBI regulates banking and monetary policy. The Trap: Option A (IRDAI) regulates insurance, not pensions. Options C and D are outside the pension-regulator remit. Cross-Exam Context: Cross-links to XII (Securities Markets), X-A (IA). SIAs generally don't engage directly with PFRDA-regulated entities on SSE, but awareness of the regulator matrix matters for scoping. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When the SE or its donor base includes NPS-corporate contributions, cite PFRDA-regulated status in the donor-profile section of your AIR. Keeps the regulator-mix explicit for downstream reviewers.
